ledger.x: 1534: King John III divides Brazil into hereditary captaincies.
1549: the General Government replaces the private captaincies.
1555: the French found France Antarctique in Guanabara Bay.
1567: the last French settlers are expelled from Guanabara Bay.
1580: the Iberian Union puts the Portuguese crown, and Brazil, under the Spanish Habsburgs.
1621: the Governorate General of Brazil becomes the State of Brazil.
1630: the Dutch take Recife and Olinda.
1640: the Iberian Union ends and the Portuguese crown, and Brazil, return to a separate king.
1652: the State of Maranhao is extinguished.
1654: the State of Maranhao is reconstituted as Maranhao and Grao-Para.
1654: the Dutch are expelled from Recife and Olinda.

ledger.cpn: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata

ledger.x: 1815 (16 December): Brazil becomes a kingdom in union with Portugal.
1816 (August): Portuguese-Brazilian troops invade the Banda Oriental.
1821 (18 July): the Banda Oriental is annexed.
1821: Cisplatina becomes a province of Brazil.

wars.name: France Antarctique (Mem de Sa's war)
wars.outcome: The French colony at Guanabara Bay founded in 1555 was attacked in 1560; the last French settlers were expelled in 1567.

wars.name: Dutch-Portuguese War in Brazil
wars.outcome: The Dutch held Recife and Olinda from 1630 to 1654.

wars.name: Guarani War and the Treaty of Madrid
wars.outcome: The Guarani refused the transfer of the Misiones Orientales; the war of 1756 and the Jesuits' resistance 'led to the nullification of the treaty by the subsequent Treaty of El Pardo' (1761).

wars.name: War of the Oranges
wars.outcome: Badajoz (6 June 1801) and Madrid (29 September 1801): Portugal ceded Olivenza; the Misiones Orientales stayed Portuguese.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Banda Oriental
wars.outcome: Montevideo was occupied on 20 January 1817; the countryside was fought over for about three years; the province was annexed in 1821.

certainty.note: No surveyed frontiers: the coast and the Tordesillas line were never mapped; bandeirante expansion is undated.
The 1750 and 1777 lines follow rivers (Uruguay, Iguacu, Parana, Paraguay, Guapore, Madeira, Javary) but the interior was unsurveyed; the Rio Grande and Misiones frontier is sharper after 1801.
